notes: All examples are fake and safe for hackathon demos.
No real patient information is stored here.

fever.recommendation: Rest, hydrate, and monitor for new or worsening symptoms.

cough.recommendation: Use supportive care and watch for breathing trouble or chest pain.

headache.recommendation: Hydrate, rest in a quiet room, and track whether the pain changes pattern.

stomach pain.recommendation: Try bland foods, hydrate, and avoid heavy meals until symptoms settle.

chest pain.recommendation: Treat this as urgent if the pain is severe, sudden, or paired with breathing trouble.

symptom_default.recommendation: Use supportive care and reassess if it continues beyond 24 to 48 hours.

paracetamol.usage: Used for fever and mild to moderate pain relief.
paracetamol.dosage: Follow the label or clinician guidance. Typical adult doses are spaced several hours apart.
warnings: Do not combine with other products containing acetaminophen.
Avoid exceeding the daily maximum dose.
Check liver safety if you have liver disease.

ibuprofen.usage: Used for pain, inflammation, and fever reduction.
ibuprofen.dosage: Take with food and only as directed on the label or by a clinician.
warnings: Avoid if you have active stomach ulcer symptoms.
Do not combine with other NSAIDs unless told to do so.

cetirizine.usage: Used for allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and itching.
cetirizine.dosage: Usually taken once daily, but follow the package or clinical instructions.
warnings: May cause drowsiness in some people.
Be careful when driving until you know how it affects you.

omeprazole.usage: Used for acid reflux and stomach acid symptoms.
omeprazole.dosage: Usually taken before meals, but follow the package or clinician guidance.
warnings: Use only as directed if symptoms last longer than the label suggests.
Check with a clinician if you have ongoing stomach pain or weight loss.

diet_suggestions: Keep carbohydrates steady across the day.
Choose fiber-rich meals with vegetables, beans, and whole grains.
Pair carbs with protein to slow glucose spikes.
hydration_tips: Choose water most of the time.
Keep a bottle nearby and sip regularly.

diet_suggestions: Aim for lower sodium and more fresh foods.
Build meals around produce, legumes, and lean protein.
hydration_tips: Watch caffeine if it makes you feel off.

diet_suggestions: Try smaller meals and avoid late-night heavy eating.
Notice which foods trigger symptoms for you.
Stay upright after meals when possible.
hydration_tips: Avoid lying down immediately after eating.

diet_suggestions: Increase soluble fiber and reduce saturated fat.
Build more plant-forward meals into the week.
Use fish, beans, and oats as helpful staples.
hydration_tips: Water and unsweetened beverages are a good default.

guidance: Pause and take a slower breath than usual.
Shrink the task to the next manageable step.
Reach out to a trusted person if your mind feels overloaded.
calming_suggestions: Name five things you can see.
Exhale longer than you inhale three times.

guidance: Anxiety can make the moment feel bigger than it is.
Keep your focus on one small action.
A short walk or a glass of water can help reset the pace.
calming_suggestions: Plant both feet on the floor.
Notice the temperature of the room.

guidance: You do not need to solve everything today.
Gentle structure helps when energy is low.
A small meal, shower, or message to someone safe can be enough for now.
calming_suggestions: Sit near daylight for a few minutes.
Write down one thing that felt okay today.

guidance: Reduce the number of decisions in front of you.
Choose one thing to pause and one thing to finish.
Let support be practical, not perfect.
calming_suggestions: Take 60 seconds away from the screen.
Return with a single next step.
